newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas seen still on the retreat at open.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas seen still on the retreat at open.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Wednesday in continuance of Tuesday's correction as traders took profits and cash prices spiraled downward.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.39 to $2.42 after settling to the downside Tuesday at $2.475 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September last traded 4.5 cents lower at $2.43.
Early Wednesday cash prices were talked several cents lower in the high-$2.30s at Henry Hub and at $2.47 at Chicago city-gate.

Weighing heavily on cash have been the cooler-than-normal temperatures across most of the East and Midwest this week, with rains also dampening cooling demand in parts of the Southwest following a few days of record heat. Warmer weather is forecast to return to most of the eastern half of the U.S. this weekend, according to Weather Services Corp.

Technically, September support was pegged at the 10-day moving average at $2.368, and then at the 20-day moving average at $2.24. Further support was seen near $2.20. Traders said resistance was first at the new high of $2.605, with further selling likely at $2.64-2.655.
In Tuesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices rose three cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were unchanged in the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas was up slightly in the mid-$2.70s.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report range from 60 to 90 bcf versus an 80 bcf build for the same week last year.

On the nuclear side, the 610 megawatt (MW) Oyster Creek unit is expected to return to the grid today, while ConEd's 975 MW Indian Point 2 unit was set to restart later today, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
